organisations.name: Example Kilkenny Family Practice
organisations.description: Private general practice in Kilkenny with four GPs registered with the Irish Medical Council, two practice nurses and three administrative staff. Patients attend as private fee-paying patients under the practice's terms of care. All staff sign confidentiality agreements. No operations outside Ireland.

organisations.name: Example Praxiscloud GmbH
organisations.description: Munich company hosting electronic patient record software for medical practices. Hosts data only in its own data centres in Frankfurt and Nuremberg. Its support staff are in Germany. It has no establishment, staff or sub-processor outside the EEA.

transfer.title: GP practice moves its electronic patient record to a German-hosted cloud system

data.description: The practice's full electronic patient record: names, addresses, dates of birth, PPS numbers, consultation notes, diagnoses, prescriptions, test results and correspondence.

transfer.purpose_description: Hosting the record the GPs and nurses use to diagnose, treat and follow up the practice's patients, replacing the on-premises server.
transfer.necessity: The record is the practice's working clinical file; it must be complete and available to clinicians at every consultation. The provider hosts and maintains it and does not use it for its own purposes.
transfer.retention: Records are kept for the practice's retention schedule (8 years after last contact for adults; until age 25 for children). On termination the provider returns all data and deletes its copies within 30 days.
transfer.onward: One sub-processor (backup storage, Germany) approved in writing by the practice; no others without prior written authorisation.
transfer.method: One-off encrypted migration from the old server, then daily use over TLS from the practice's network with per-user accounts.
transfer.additional_info: The practice's patients include about 1,300 children. The provider's German support staff access records only on a ticket raised by the practice, and each access is logged.

evidence.title: Data processing agreement (Art 28)
evidence.summary: Provider processes only on the practice's documented instructions; personnel confidentiality; Art 32 security; written authorisation for sub-processors (one approved: backup storage in Germany) with the same obligations; assistance with rights requests, breach notification and DPIAs; return and deletion on termination; audits and inspections; no transfers outside the EEA.

evidence.title: ISO/IEC 27001 certificate
evidence.summary: Certification of the provider's information security management system covering EHR hosting at both German data centres, issued by an accredited certification body.

evidence.title: DPIA for the cloud EHR migration
evidence.summary: Assesses moving the full record of about 6,500 patients, including children, to the provider; risks of unauthorised access, loss of availability, provider access and migration errors; measures: encryption, MFA, logged ticket-based support access, daily backups, tested restore, return and deletion on exit. Residual risk acceptable. Completed before migration.

evidence.title: Practice access and security procedure
evidence.summary: Named accounts with MFA for every clinician and staff member, role-based access, encryption in transit and at rest, access logs reviewed monthly by the practice manager, daily backups with a quarterly restore test.

evidence.title: Patient privacy notice
evidence.summary: Updated notice on the practice website and in the waiting room: identity and contact of the practice and its DPO, purposes and legal bases, the German hosting provider as processor, no transfers outside the EEA, retention periods, patients' rights and how to exercise them, the right to complain to the Data Protection Commission.

evidence.title: Record of processing activities
evidence.summary: The practice's Art 30 record, updated to list the cloud EHR hosting, the provider and its sub-processor, the data categories, storage in Germany, retention periods and security measures.

evidence.title: Clinical responsibility for the record
evidence.summary: All clinical processing of the record is carried out by or under the responsibility of the practice's GPs, each registered with the Irish Medical Council; nurses and administrative staff work under the GPs' direction and sign confidentiality agreements. Signed by the senior partner.

look_for: HIPAA is not routed: no party, person or storage is in the US.
No Chapter V transfer: Germany is in the EEA and the provider has no access, staff or sub-processor outside it.
Controller and processor derived from 'processes only on the practice's documented instructions'; the Art 28 agreement covers the required terms.
Art 6: a private practice is not a public authority, so 6(1)(e) is not the route; the care relationship with fee-paying patients points to 6(1)(b).
Art 9(2)(h) with Irish s.52(1)(c)-(d) and s.52(2)(a): processing by or under the responsibility of GPs registered with the Irish Medical Council.
Art 9(3): the GPs' professional secrecy. The corpus has no Medical Council rules, so watch whether this is settled from the facts or left open as law not in sources.
DPIA, security, transparency and records are each backed by a supplied evidence item and should be met without asking for proof beyond the summaries.
expected.note: Author's expectation in the two-layer input shape, not validated by a live assessment and not a legal compliance claim. Built to exercise the intra-EEA path: no Chapter V, no HIPAA, no public-task basis.
